study type: Case-control study nested within a cohort
exposure: Prenatal exposure to 33 consumer product chemicals (organophosphate ester flame retardant [OPE] metabolites, phthalate metabolites, phenols)
cohort: The participants were newborns classified as small-for-gestational age (N=31), large-for-gestational age (N=28), and appropriate for gestational age (N=31) controls, selected from the larger LIFECODES cohort.
finding: Joint prenatal exposure to organophosphate ester flame retardants (OPEs) and phthalates was associated with lower odds of delivering a large-for-gestational age (LGA) infant.
birth_weight: Not explicitly stated as a weight range, but babies were categorized as small-for-gestational age (SGA), large-for-gestational age (LGA), or appropriate for gestational age (AGA).
gest_age: Not explicitly stated as a range, but babies were categorized based on their size for gestational age (SGA, LGA, AGA).
